scope: New findings only (5 security + 4 spec-conformance). Re-seen/still-open, fix-pending (Q-21 re-weigh), carry-overs and manual-review parked items are not re-classified here. No regressions this run.

labelNumbering.convention: Ledger sequences continued. Informational items are bundled into the Q- sequence (precedent: Q-21 is severity 'informational' with a Q label). F labels use F-NN-<story>.

classifiedFindings.label: L-26
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Borderline Low/Medium. The case for Medium: the DoS is permanent for this escrow, costs the griefer 1 wei plus gas, and the escrow cannot run the recovery that L-24's wont-fix rationale depended on. The case for Low, which is the classification: no asset is at risk (abort() is fork-proven to restore the old pooler fully); no ongoing protocol function is impaired (the old pooler keeps working after abort, and the canonical pair and UniPoolerV2 stay usable through a mint-path seed, fork-proven); the cost is delay plus redeploying a differently-shaped one-off seeder. Precedents L-24 (same primitive, owner wont-fix: 'a mild inconvenience at most') and phStaging run-39 L-01 (Low) are both Low. A human may re-apply L-24's wont-fix, but should do so knowing the escrow lacks the mint-path recovery L-24 assumed.

classification.assetImpact: None. The escrow's BPT/sUSDS/phUSD/USDS go back to the old pooler through abort() (fork-proven under a normal pool, a paused pool and a paused vault). The impact is that this escrow's exitAndSeed can never succeed, so the one-off cutover is delayed until a replacement seeder is deployed and reviewed.
attackPath: 1. The canonical sUSDS/phUSD V2 pair is public from createPair onward. UniPoolerV2's constructor requires it, and the escrow reads newPooler.pair() at construction, so the window spans several broadcast txs.
2. Griefer: sUSDS.transfer(pair, 1) + pair.sync() (or a dust pair.mint).

3. exitAndSeed -> _requireEmptyPair reverts PairNotEmpty(1,0,1,0). This holds permanently, because the escrow seeds only via Router02 behind a strict reserves==(0,0) gate and has no mint-path branch. Redeploying the same escrow fails the same way.

4. Operator calls abort(). Funds return to the old pooler. Recovery requires a different contract that seeds through transfer + pair.mint(newPooler) with a reserve-ratio assertion (fork: the mint path absorbs the dust).
classification.likelihood: medium. Cost is negligible and the call is permissionless, but the griefer gains nothing and must act inside the cutover window.
classification.assumptions: The canonical pair is created in a separate, publicly visible tx before exitAndSeed (structural under story-103's multi-tx --slow broadcast).
classification.externalRequirements: An external griefer who watches for the pair's creation.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 Medium needs the protocol's function or availability to be impaired, or value to leak. Neither holds here. The only thing bricked is a one-off migration helper, and abort() returns the full status quo, so all protocol functions (old pooler dispatch, UniPoolerV2, the canonical pair) keep working. The cost is operational delay plus a redeploy of a mint-path seeder, which is exactly the 'delay on a one-off cutover' tier the owner judged in L-24 and the reason phStaging run-39 L-01 is Low. Severity is the same as L-24. What is new is the locus: L-24's wont-fix assumed the safe recovery 'direct transfer + pair.mint with a reserve-ratio assertion' was available, and this escrow cannot execute it. That is why this is a separate Low and is not suppressed under L-24. PATTERN-001's mechanical 'potential-high' (first-depositor mapping) did not set the label: no inflation or theft is possible, since the gate reverts before any value moves.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: When IUniswapV2Pair(pair).totalSupply()==0, seed via safeTransfer of both sides to the pair plus pair.mint(newPooler) instead of Router02. Replace the strict-empty gate with a dust-tolerant reserve-ratio and LP post-check. Otherwise, phStaging2 story-103/108 must document the abort-and-redeploy-a-mint-path-seeder runbook before broadcast.
classifiedFindings.storyTag: story-052 (review/) asks the auditor to evaluate ('DoS only; abort returns funds'). That claim is confirmed, but abort is not a recovery: this escrow cannot complete the cutover.

classifiedFindings.label: L-27
classifiedFindings.plausibility: implausible as an attack (no external actor); plausible only as an owner sequencing slip outside the runbook
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Permanent loss of whatever withdrawBPT sends after a repoint could argue for Medium under Law 3 ('up to High if it enables direct asset loss'). Held at Low because it needs two owner calls that story-103 does not contain (setPool, then withdrawBPT to the escrow), and the original BPT is never at risk because it stays on the old pooler, where rescueERC20 can reach it.

classification.assetImpact: Tokens of the new pool X that the owner sends to the escrow via withdrawBPT after BalancerPoolerV2.setPool(X) are permanently stranded. exitAndSeed reverts NoBPT, abort() moves only the snapshot _bpt/_sUSDS/_phUSD/_usds, and the escrow has no owner or rescue. The original BPT is not affected.
attackPath: 1. The escrow is deployed and snapshots _bpt = oldPooler.pool() (immutable, L199/L217).
2. The owner calls BalancerPoolerV2.setPool(X) for an unrelated reason.
3. The owner calls withdrawBPT(escrow, n), which transfers token X to the escrow.
4. exitAndSeed reverts NoBPT. abort() returns nothing of X, so X is stranded forever.
classification.likelihood: low. Not on the story-103 path, and BalancerPoolerV2 is being retired (story-050).
classification.assumptions: A non-malicious owner repoints the old pooler between escrow deploy and withdrawBPT.

classifiedFindings.justification: Law-3 footgun, not a malicious-owner vector. A competent owner would not expect the escrow to bind silently to the pre-repoint BPT, or that abort() cannot return the token withdrawBPT just delivered. Surprise means footgun, which means in scope at honest severity. The impact is real, permanent stranding, but it is reachable only through an owner sequence that the runbook does not contain, and the main asset (the original BPT) stays recoverable on the old pooler. That is Low with footgun guidance. It is not Medium, since there is no external path and protocol availability is unaffected. Fork-proven by test_run22_setPoolAfterDeploy_strandsNewPoolTokenInEscrow.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Safe-config guidance: in UniPoolerCutoverCore, assert oldPooler.pool() == escrow.bpt() in the same broadcast immediately before withdrawBPT(escrow, bal), and never call setPool on the old pooler while an escrow is live. Code-side option: have abort() also return oldPooler.pool() via _returnAll, or expose a bpt-match check.
classifiedFindings.relatedManualReview: PATTERN-MR-003 (generic no-rescue stranding) stays parked separately.

classifiedFindings.label: L-28
classifiedFindings.plausibility: plausible (any Balancer swapper; organic flow can trip it too)
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Borderline Low/QA. The revert is temporary, and both retry and abort are available, so it could be QA. Kept at Low because the runbook's own 'tight tolerance' advice maximises griefability while buying no economic protection (ECON-001), and a mid-broadcast revert poisons the story-103 progress file. That is a concrete operational hazard with a cheap fix.

classification.assetImpact: None. exitAndSeed is atomic, the BPT stays in the escrow, and the operator can re-quote and retry or abort(). The impact is repeated liveness denial of the cutover at about $0.03 per attempt, plus a mid-broadcast revert that leaves the forge progress file inconsistent.
attackPath: 1. story-103 broadcasts exitAndSeed through the public mempool (--broadcast --slow, no private relay) with floors set to the live proportional share minus a tight tolerance (1 bp in repo).
2. A griefer front-runs with a Balancer swap of ~4 sUSDS->phUSD that moves one side past the tolerance.
4. The griefer unwinds at a ~0.024 sUSDS round trip. Repeatable per attempt.
classification.likelihood: low-medium. Cheap, but the griefer gains nothing. Organic flow during a slow multi-tx broadcast can trip it with no attacker at all.
classification.assumptions: Floors are set at the runbook's tight tolerance and the tx goes through the public mempool.
classification.externalRequirements: A mempool-watching griefer, or organic Balancer flow inside the broadcast window.

classifiedFindings.justification: Temporary, retriable availability griefing of a one-off migration, with no value at risk. C4 Medium needs protocol function or availability impact beyond a recoverable, operator-mitigable delay, so this is not Medium. It sits above QA because the operator-gate design rationale in story-052 is inaccurate (spec half routed as F-01-052) and the tight-tolerance configuration is a non-obvious operational footgun: a competent operator would expect tighter floors to be strictly safer, but ECON-001 proves a loose floor gives up no value on two 50/50 constant-product venues.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Size the exit tolerance for griefing resistance (e.g. 0.5-1%), not tight. ECON-001 shows sandwiching is net-negative at 1% and 5%. Use a private relay for exitAndSeed if available. Document that floor reverts are expected and recoverable, and how the progress file resumes after an exitAndSeed revert.
classifiedFindings.evidence: ECON-002 fork test at 1 bp tolerance (block 26136000).

classifiedFindings.label: Q-24

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated. On fork, a sandwich that skews the Balancer pool inside the floors is net-negative for the attacker (-1.753 sUSDS at 1% tol, -8.808 sUSDS at 5%). The protocol's seeded invariant rises slightly (+0.96 / +4.82 sUSDS at p0).
classification.assumptions: The Balancer pool stays a hookless 50/50 weighted pool with a 0.3% fee (verified on-chain). A pool type with a different curve or hooks would reopen the question.

classifiedFindings.justification: On-chain validation of minAmountsOut is minimal: length==2 and >0, so 1 wei passes and token order is unvalidated. The seed inherits the Balancer spot composition with no ratio or peg band. These are spec and defense-in-depth gaps, not a value leak: two constant-product venues mean the back-arbitrage returns only the attacker's own slippage minus fees, and POL is not extracted (ECON-001, CODE-003). Per the L-22/L-06 tolerance precedent, the floors bound accepted MEV on protocol-owned liquidity. Not suppressed under L-06 because L-06's own triageReason says new code reusing the pool should be revisited. It was revisited here and the conclusion is QA. PATTERN-002/003's mechanical 'potential-high' did not set the label.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: In UniPoolerCutoverCore, assert getPoolTokenInfo order == [sUSDS, phUSD] when building minAmountsOut. Optionally add an on-chain ratio band on the seed.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-25

classification.assetImpact: Opportunity cost only. After the cutover, the third party's 37.1% Balancer remainder (11,007 sUSDS / 13,249 phUSD) stays a live second venue at the same price, so part of a Stage-4 peg lift is arbitraged into it: about $11 at Δ*=1,540 sUSDS, with V2 settling at $0.9735 instead of $1, or about $8 in the stray-sUSDS variant.
classification.assumptions: Balancer swaps on the remainder stay enabled after the cutover.

classifiedFindings.justification: Opportunity cost on protocol-owned liquidity, not a value leak (project rule: over-payment or misallocation of externally-derived yield is opportunity cost). The amount is $8-$11 and nobody is harmed. Informational, bundled into QA per the Q-21 precedent. It is distinct from Q-21, which is about plan §5 zap sizing against seeded depth.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Note in story-103 / plan §5 that the 37.1% Balancer remainder absorbs part of the peg lift until swaps stop or the LP exits, and resize Stage-4 zap chunks for the combined depth.

classifiedFindings.label: F-01-052
classifiedFindings.justification: The code faithfully implements the design, but story-052's security rationale is inaccurate: it says the immutable-operator gate prevents a mid-cutover front-run revert, and the dominant revert vector (a Balancer swap past the tight floor) bypasses the gate. The story's intent is not unsafe (atomic tx, abort/retry, no value extractable), so it is not escalated as an unsafe story. Rated Low rather than Info because the inaccurate rationale drives a runbook choice ('tight tolerance') that maximises griefability. Security half is L-28.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Amend story-052/103: floor-tolerance reverts are expected and recoverable; size tolerance for griefing resistance; specify broadcast grouping and progress-file resume after an exitAndSeed revert.

classifiedFindings.label: F-02-052
classifiedFindings.humanFlag: Human-only decision: story-052's tax/accounting rationale for routing the owner's 202.30 BPT through the escrow is already unmet, because that tranche was exited and burned at block 25,985,119 (tx 0xd8ecb3be...). The story-103 L199 fork-test checklist item cannot be satisfied, which is a cross-project /audit-script concern.
classifiedFindings.justification: The story asserts on-chain state that is false ('The owner already holds 202.30 BPT'). Following it as written fails loudly: floors sized on the combined 20,604.1 BPT exceed the true share by 0.99%, so exitAndSeed reverts at any tolerance below 0.99%, and a hardcoded transfer of 202.30e18 reverts. No value is lost (ECON-005). Low, because the deviation would block the cutover runbook as specified and needs story amendment before execution.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Drop the owner->escrow BPT transfer from 052/103, or make it a live-read that is allowed to be zero and logs the zero. Size floors on the escrow's actual balance (20,401.809 BPT). Restate L199.

classifiedFindings.label: F-03-052
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Overlaps Q-21 (fix-pending). Kept as its own F entry because its subject, an unenforced human seed-price confirmation, differs from Q-21's sizing numbers. The human may fold it into Q-21.
classifiedFindings.justification: Story-052's human seed-price confirmation is not carried into any enforced gate, and the plan figures it would be checked against are stale by about 2.7x (Δ* ~$1,712 vs plan's ~$636-640; ECON-003). The seed is fair market and the gap is the phUSD discount, so no value is at risk. Informational.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Promote the seed-price confirmation into 052's Required Human Action list or a 103 gate. Mark plan §5 as illustrative-at-block-26,093,540. Do not close Q-21 on story-108's $638.

classifiedFindings.label: F-04-052
classifiedFindings.humanFlag: Landed on master (0fd6bdf) while story-052 sits in review/ with two checklist items unticked. story-052 L10: the escrow must not be deployed to mainnet before the audit passes; story-103 L185 gates on 052 reaching complete/ or auto-complete/.
classifiedFindings.justification: Process and state deviation, not a code deviation. The landed-while-in-review flag is required by the story policy. The gate in story-103 correctly blocks execution, so this is informational.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Resolve F-02-052 and F-03-052 text amendments (and L-26's recovery decision) before moving story-052 to complete/.

summary.headline: 0 H/M. Three Lows on the new UniPoolerCutoverEscrow: L-26 is permanent but fund-safe dust-poisoning DoS of exitAndSeed (borderline Medium, held Low per L-24/phStaging run-39 L-01); L-27 is a stale-_bpt setPool owner footgun; L-28 is tight-floor griefing. Two QA items: Q-24 off-chain-only floors (value leak refuted on fork) and Q-25 cross-venue arb opportunity cost. Four story-052 spec-conformance items, F-01..F-04-052.

notesForDownstream: Mechanical 'potential-high' hints (PATTERN-001, PATTERN-002/003) were not used for labels; both were refuted or bounded with fork evidence.
L-26 is a disclosed re-raise adjacent to owner wont-fix L-24. The report must quote L-24's triageReason and state the new fact: the escrow cannot run L-24's prescribed mint-path recovery.
No High/Medium, so no individual submissions or PoC requirement. L-26/L-27/L-28/Q-24/Q-25 go to qa-report.md. F-01..F-04-052 go to spec-conformance.md only.
Q-21 re-weigh (fix-pending) is handled in reconciliation and is not re-labelled here.
